whatThePageStates: The page is a catalogue of the AWS Managed Rules rule groups that AWS WAF publishes for specific application use cases. It has six H2 sections, one per rule group: SQL database (AWSManagedRulesSQLiRuleSet, WCU 200), Linux operating system (AWSManagedRulesLinuxRuleSet, WCU 200), POSIX operating system (AWSManagedRulesUnixRuleSet, WCU 100), Windows operating system (AWSManagedRulesWindowsRuleSet, WCU 200), PHP application (AWSManagedRulesPHPRuleSet, WCU 100) and WordPress application (AWSManagedRulesWordPressRuleSet, WCU 100). Each section gives the vendor name, rule-group name, WCU cost, a boilerplate note about versions, a paragraph on when to evaluate the group, a labelling paragraph, and a two-column table of the individual rules with their description, rule action and label. Every statement is presence-only: the page names what exists and what each rule inspects. It never says a rule group, rule, region, service or resource type is unsupported, and it contains no Yes/No/Partial matrix of any kind.

features.featureName: Use-case specific AWS Managed Rules rule groups
features.collapse: The page's table rows are individual rules, not rule groups. There are 28 rule rows across six tables (SQL database 8, Linux 3, POSIX 3, Windows 8, PHP 4, WordPress 2). Each table sits under an H2 that names one rule group, so all 28 rows collapse onto 6 distinct managed rule groups. The rule-group identity is carried by the heading and by the label prefix inside each row (awswaf:managed:aws:sql-database, :linux-os, :posix-os, :windows-os, :php-app, :wordpress-app), never by a column of its own. A parser that counts table rows gets 28; the number of catalogue entries this page actually claims is 6.
features.statuses: Presence-only, single state. Rule-group level: 6 listed, all published and available; 6 Yes, 0 No, 0 Partial; 6+0+0=6. Row level: 28 rules; 8 SQL database + 3 Linux + 3 POSIX + 8 Windows + 4 PHP + 2 WordPress = 28, and each of the 28 rows states 'Rule action: Block'. There is no No column, no 'isn't available' sentence, and no exclusion note anywhere on the page, so not-supported is never STATED — only absent. There is nothing tri-state: 'Block' is the configured action of every rule, not a Partial coverage value, and treating action variation as a status would be wrong because it does not vary here.
features.scope: None. There is no second dimension. The rule groups are not qualified by Region, by plan, by scan method or by scope (AWS WAF's own CLOUDFRONT vs REGIONAL scope distinction is not mentioned on this page at all). WCU cost per rule group (200/200/100/200/100/100) is a capacity figure, not a scope. The body-size limits quoted inside eight rule descriptions do vary by resource type (8 KB fixed for Application Load Balancer and AWS AppSync; 16 KB default, raisable to 64 KB, for CloudFront, API Gateway, Amazon Cognito, App Runner, Verified Access and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway), but that is an inspection-size quota attached to a rule, not a per-resource-type availability scope for the rule groups.
features.reasoning: managedRuleGroup is the right axis because the page's unit of claim is the rule group: it is what AWS publishes, what a customer adds to a web ACL, what has a VendorName/Name/WCU triple, and what each H2 enumerates. It is a catalogue axis because the list is AWS WAF's own published inventory, not a universe that exists independently of the service. The individual rules are the internal composition of each catalogue entry, one level below the coverage claim — you cannot subscribe to SQLi_BODY on its own — which is why they are recorded as the row count that collapses rather than as the axis. The page is explicitly the 'use-case specific' subset of AWS Managed Rules; the baseline, bot-control, IP-reputation and other rule groups live on sibling pages, so 6 is this page's complete claim and not a fragment of a larger table.

shouldNotExtract: The rule names themselves as a coverage axis (28 of them) — they are the contents of six products, not six-plus-twenty-two supported things. The repeated per-section 'Note' block about static versions, the changelog link and DescribeManagedRuleGroup — identical boilerplate in all six sections, not a claim. WCU values (200, 200, 100, 200, 100, 100) — capacity units, a quota. VendorName 'AWS' repeated six times. The body-size limits (8 KB, 16 KB, 64 KB, first 8 KB of headers, first 200 headers) and the 'Continue' oversize-content-handling option — quotas and configuration defaults. The label strings (awswaf:managed:aws:...) — identifiers, useful only for attributing a row to its rule group. 'Rule action: Block' — a default action, not a coverage status. Example attack patterns (/proc/version, echo $HOME, echo $PATH, ||nslookup, ;cmd, Invoke-Expression, fsockopen, $_GET, do-reset-wordpress, xmlrpc.php) — illustrations. The prose OS list in the POSIX section ('Linux, AIX, HP-UX, macOS, Solaris, FreeBSD, and OpenBSD') — applicability guidance, not an enumerated support matrix. Cross-references between sections ('use in conjunction with'). The console-experience banner at the top, the anchor tags, and the entire 'See also' AI-coding-assistant / Agent Toolkit boilerplate at the bottom.
coverageDimensions: REGION: nothing. The page names no Region, no Region count, no partition, and no Region-availability statement. Any per-Region figure attributed to this page is fabricated. SERVICE: nothing as coverage. The only AWS service the page is about is AWS WAF itself. Eight other service or resource names appear (Application Load Balancer, AWS AppSync, CloudFront, API Gateway, Amazon Cognito, App Runner, Verified Access, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway), but they occur only inside repeated body-size-limit sentences in eight rule descriptions — they say how many kilobytes of the body a rule reads, not which services these rule groups protect. Reading '8 services covered' off this page would be a fabrication built from a quota sentence. RESOURCE TYPE: nothing as a coverage enumeration; 'resource type' appears only in the phrase 'the body size limit for the protection pack (web ACL) and resource type', with the eight names above as illustration. The single dimension this page genuinely supplies is the managed-rule-group catalogue: 6 use-case specific rule groups, with 28 constituent rules.
trap: The single most likely misparse is counting table rows and reporting 28 supported items, because the page has six separate tables whose rows are rules while the actual catalogue entry is the rule group named in the H2 above each table — the axis value never appears in a column, so a row-oriented parser cannot see the collapse. Runners-up: (1) harvesting the eight service names out of the repeated body-size-limit sentence and reporting an 8-service or 8-resource-type coverage matrix, when that sentence is a quota; (2) harvesting the POSIX prose list 'Linux, AIX, HP-UX, macOS, Solaris, FreeBSD, and OpenBSD' as a 7-value operatingSystem support axis, when it is advice about when to evaluate one rule group; (3) inventing a status axis out of 'Rule action: Block', which is identical in all 28 rows and is a default action rather than Yes/No/Partial; (4) treating the absence of any rule group as a stated No — nothing on this page is ever marked unsupported, so a No count from here is always zero; (5) mistaking this page for the whole AWS Managed Rules catalogue and flagging the missing baseline, bot-control, ATP, ACFP and IP-reputation groups as gaps, when they are simply documented on sibling pages; (6) double-counting the six WCU/VendorName lines or the six identical Note blocks as data rows.
